boat.text:
A fishing hull, low in the water, carrying a household and what it could lift. A woman at the stern has a child asleep against her shoulder and a bundle of tools at her feet.

They are not in distress. They are simply going somewhere, slowly, with too much weight.

water.text: The water goes into a jar that is already half full of something else. The woman says a word you do not know and touches her forehead, and the boats drift apart.

choices.text: Watch them until they are small.

bound.text:
"Ugarit. My cousin has a roof." She says it as a fact she has rehearsed. "Inland is finished for us this year."

The master says nothing until they are out of earshot. "There will be more of them by the autumn."

away.text: You look at the water instead. The master looks at you, and then at the sail, and then at the water, and the boat goes on.

sources: Local displacement in the Late Bronze Age Levant, general
provenance.notes: Invented scene. Movement of households for a failed harvest is plausible and is not the later collapse.
